text:
Maya (People Ops): Heads up  member had an emergency extraction + root canal in Lisbon. Clinic asked if Redwood can pay them directly (they prefer IBAN in EUR) and requested we send an EOB to the member with all PHI redacted except codes + amounts. Claim 2026-PT-3344. Who owns the EFT flow and what docs do we need to collect?

Ellen (Benefits): We support direct-bill for dental if it meets plan coverage rules. Required: signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB), patient consent for any redaction, itemized invoice (with local procedure codes and service dates), and provider tax ID.

Ravi (Finance): For EU wires we need full bank details (IBAN, BIC/SWIFT), beneficiary name exactly as on bank account, and a scanned bank mandate/remit form. Also provider VAT number if they charge VAT.

Maya (People Ops): Clinic asked for a one-page checklist they can fill. Can someone paste a short provider-facing checklist/email I can forward?

Ellen (Benefits): Paste below  short provider email + checklist:

To: billing@clinic.pt
Subject: Redwood Inference  Direct Billing Request for [MemberName] (Claim 2026-PT-3344)

Hello,

Thank you for agreeing to direct-bill. To process payment please provide the following scanned documents: 
1) Signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB) from the patient (PDF)
2) Patient-signed consent authorizing Redwood to redact PHI on the EOB if requested
3) Itemized invoice in EUR showing procedure codes, service dates, and amounts
4) Provider tax/VAT registration (scanned)
5) Banking details: IBAN, BIC/SWIFT, account holder name, and remittance instructions
6) Billing contact name and billing email/phone

Please indicate if you accept payment in USD to expedite settlement and include net-of-VAT amount if applicable. Send all materials to claims@redwood.com and reference Claim 2026-PT-3344.

Best regards,
Redwood Claims Team

Ravi (Finance): Add this tiny note for AP: "If invoice includes VAT, please show VAT line. If you prefer net payment, state net amount and VAT separately."

Maya (People Ops): Thanks  forwarding now. About the EOB redaction question: clinic wants everything removed except codes and amounts before the member sees it. Is that allowed?

Ellen (Benefits): We can redact identifiers (SSN, national ID, address) with explicit member consent, but we must retain dates of service, procedure codes, and charge amounts on the EOB for compliance and audit. Removing service dates or codes is not permitted. If the clinic requests more redaction we need legal sign-off.

ClaimsBot: Automated: International direct-bill workflow initiated. Manual review required. Expected adjudication 5-10 business days after complete docs received.

Ravi (Finance): Timing note: once claims confirms docs and AOB, finance validates banking (1-3 business days) then initiates SEPA/FX transfer (2-5 business days standard). USD option often clears faster in our corridors.

Maya (People Ops): Great. I'll include the AOB snippet and the consent language. Can you paste a 1-line AOB we can ask the member to sign?

Ellen (Benefits): AOB snippet: "I, [MemberName], assign payment for services related to claim 2026-PT-3344 to [ProviderName] and authorize Redwood Inference to pay the provider directly. I consent to Redwood redacting identifying information on the EOB as described above."

Maya (People Ops): Perfect. I'll send and update here when provider replies. :thumbsup: (End of thread)
